topic: Voice-Driven Murder Mystery: Building Conversational AI Games

key_points: Shadowlight is a voice-driven murder mystery and heist game played inside Minecraft (24 HN points)
Players use natural voice to interrogate NPCs who are powered by LLMs with Speech-to-Text -> LLM -> Text-to-Speech pipeline
HN community feedback: 'It is so easy to grow attached to the NPCs when you can talk to them' — emotional attachment to AI NPCs is the standout hook
Shows the pattern of embedding conversational AI games inside an existing sandbox world rather than building from scratch
Gron Games is a murder mystery game built on an open-source generative-AI agent framework (43 HN points)
Demonstrates that you can build a full AI game using an existing agent framework rather than wiring LLMs from scratch
Open-source angle appeals to indie devs who want a template for AI-driven game logic
AI murder mystery game where the LLM dynamically generates cases and suspects (4 HN points)
Focuses on procedural mystery generation plus clue collection and reasoning
Represents the pure web-based (non-voice) end of the conversational AI game spectrum
Mantella is a Skyrim and Fallout 4 mod (400 GitHub stars) that lets you naturally speak to NPCs
Core pipeline: Speech-to-Text -> LLMs -> Text-to-Speech, the reference architecture for voice-driven NPC conversation
Proves the STT->LLM->TTS loop is the standard building block for conversational AI games
Runs fully local — shows privacy and cost advantages of local models
Whodunit demonstrates using LLMs to author and run murder mystery games with dynamic suspects and hidden identities
Highlights the challenge of keeping story coherence and not leaking the culprit prematurely
Discusses prompt-engineering techniques to keep each NPC's knowledge consistent and secretive

stats.fact: Voice-driven murder mystery game Shadowlight (inside Minecraft) gained 24 points on Hacker News, with top community feedback being emotional attachment to voice-controlled NPCs
Gron Games, a murder mystery built on an open-source generative-AI agent framework, reached 43 points on Hacker News, showing strong indie-dev demand for AI agent framework templates
Mantella, the STT->LLM->TTS NPC dialogue mod for Skyrim and Fallout 4, has 400 GitHub stars — evidence the voice NPC pipeline is the de-facto standard for conversational AI games
The Conversational Game Theory project (aikiwiki.com) drew 121 points on Hacker News, indicating strong developer interest in the design theory behind LLM-driven interactive fiction

Noise cancellation is a major unsolved technical hurdle for voice AI agents — Krisp's article on improving turn-taking for AI voice agents drew 113 HN points, underscoring that voice UX quality is the key differentiator
LLM-driven interactive fiction is a proven genre: the 'Automating Interactive Fiction Logic Generation with LLMs' article drew 100 points on Hacker News, validating LLMs as story-logic engines

angles: Interview-style how-to: walk through building a voice-driven murder mystery using the STT->LLM->TTS pipeline, framed around the Shadowlight-in-Minecraft success story
Reference architecture: explain the voice agent loop (speech recognition, dialogue state, LLM reasoning, TTS) with concrete tool choices
Why voice beats text for mystery games: emotional attachment to NPCs and immersion you cannot get from typing
Keep the culprit secret: prompt-engineering and per-NPC memory techniques to maintain story coherence and prevent spoilers
Use an open-source agent framework (like Gron's approach) vs. building the LLM wiring from scratch — tradeoffs
Local vs cloud voice models: privacy, latency, and cost tradeoffs (Mantella's local-only approach vs. hosted APIs)
Turn-taking and interruption handling — the unsolved UX problem that separates good from bad voice games
Embedding the game inside a sandbox (Minecraft) vs. standalone web app — distribution and reach

how to build an ai game
